newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trade on Tuesday with profit-taking from retail investors seen on the market, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended up at an intraday high of 3,398 yuan ($410) per tonne, rising eight yuan. It opened at a low of 3,296 yuan.
May rose 19 yuan to 3,433, September fell seven to 3,408, the January 1998 contract put on two to 3,412 and March dropped six to 3,399.
Combined volume fell to 15,500 tonnes from 16,100.

Soybeans opened mostly up but profit-taking pushed most contracts slightly down, traders said. "Soybeans met resistance at high levels today after continued gains over the past few trading days," one trader said.
Most investors are seeking quick profits rather than long-term investment on the soybeans market, traders said.
"They sold above the 3,400-yuan level and bought at lower levels, resulting in consolidation," a second trader said.
Analysts said they expected soybeans to continue to follow a similar trend in the short term. ($1=8.2952 yuan)
